reading.body:
Dataverge operates a carrier-neutral data center in Brooklyn at 882 3rd Ave within the Industry City complex, configured to support high-density AI workloads with cabinets rated for 100 plus kilowatts each and direct access to 40 plus carriers.

The operator has not published total square footage or IT power capacity. This means the facility's actual size and its potential scale for AI deployment cannot be determined from available specifications. New York state contains 31 mapped data center facilities, but transparency about power capacity remains sparse across the region. Without published figures, this site cannot be ranked meaningfully against other AI infrastructure by scale, though its carrier-neutral design and dense cabinet specifications suggest it is intended to support power-intensive workloads.

The gap between Brooklyn's position as a dense urban market and the absence of disclosed power metrics illustrates a broader pattern. Facility operators in this region do not systematically publish the power and space data necessary to assess whether regional AI scaling is power-constrained or building-constrained. Until those figures surface, the contribution of New York's data centers to AI compute capacity remains opaque.
